records.Concise description: Open-source, self-hosted Bitcoin payment gateway software that lets merchants accept on-chain and Lightning payments without handing payment custody to a company-controlled processor.
records.Deeper researched summary: BTCPay Server is software rather than a custodial payment company. A merchant can run it against Bitcoin and Lightning infrastructure they control, create and track invoices, use point-of-sale and payment-request applications, integrate ecommerce systems, and manage refunds/payout workflows. Its official documentation describes direct peer-to-peer payment, merchant private-key control, and support for LND, Core Lightning and Eclair; third-party hosting and external integrations can still introduce additional trust assumptions.
Creators / founders: Nicolas Dorier — original creator; open-source contributors maintain the project
records.Launch / history: Created in 2017 as an open-source alternative to hosted Bitcoin payment processors and has developed into a broad self-hosted merchant-payment stack.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It is the clearest reference implementation for the distinction between payment-processing software and a company that takes custody or settles on a merchant's behalf.
Important technical or cultural characte: Self-hosted and open source
Non-custodial in the merchant-controlled deployment model
Bitcoin on-chain and Lightning invoice support
Point of sale, payment requests, plugins and ecommerce integrations
Tracks invoice state and can coordinate refunds/payouts
Trust model changes when third-party hosting or custodial integrations are used
records.Verification basis: Current official documentation and active project repository verify the payment model, self-hosted architecture, Bitcoin/Lightning support and current operation.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe BTCPay Server as a company-controlled custodial processor.
'Non-custodial' applies to the merchant-controlled deployment model; a third-party host, external wallet, Lightning backend or plugin may add separate trust assumptions.

records.Concise description: Hosted Bitcoin payment processor for on-chain and Lightning acceptance, payouts, APIs, invoicing, conversion and merchant settlement.
records.Deeper researched summary: OpenNode provides hosted checkout, APIs, plugins, invoicing, in-person payments and payouts. A charge can expose both an on-chain address and a Lightning invoice, while merchant funds are credited to an OpenNode account and can be held, converted or withdrawn/settled. That account-based flow makes OpenNode materially different from self-hosted BTCPay Server: the processor intermediates payment and settlement and may provide local-currency conversion.
records.Launch / history: Founded in the late 2010s and built specifically around Bitcoin payment processing, later adding broader business payment and payout tooling while retaining Bitcoin and Lightning as its core rails.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: OpenNode is a durable example of a hosted, Bitcoin-first processor that combines Lightning with on-chain fallback and merchant settlement/conversion.
Important technical or cultural characte: Hosted account and processor role
On-chain Bitcoin and Lightning charges
Bitcoin or supported local-currency settlement
APIs, webhooks, hosted checkout, billing and payouts
Merchant funds can be converted or withdrawn from the hosted account
records.Verification basis: Current official product and developer documentation verify active Bitcoin/Lightning processing, hosted account flows, APIs and settlement options.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not call OpenNode non-custodial in the standard hosted processing flow.
Fees, supported local currencies and jurisdictions are time-sensitive and should be reverified before public copy.

records.Entity / project type: Bitcoin payment company / custodial payment API
records.Concise description: Bitcoin payment company whose business API can send and receive over Bitcoin and Lightning while sourcing payments from supported cash or bitcoin account balances.
records.Deeper researched summary: Strike combines custodial account balances, Bitcoin/Lightning connectivity and fiat conversion/settlement infrastructure. Its current API documentation shows select business accounts can send over Lightning or on-chain Bitcoin from cash or bitcoin balances, create quotes, receive Lightning invoices, and support LNURL/Lightning-address payment flows. This profile represents Strike as one integrated payments company rather than splitting consumer app, API and cross-border products into separate entities.
records.Launch / history: Strike grew out of Zap-era Lightning payment work and developed into a consumer and business payments platform spanning Bitcoin, Lightning and fiat-connected payment flows.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: Strike demonstrates how a hosted payment service can use Lightning as a transport/settlement rail while abstracting exchange, balances and cross-border payment operations behind an account and API.
Important technical or cultural characte: Custodial account balances
Bitcoin on-chain and Lightning sending/receiving
Quote-based conversion between supported account currencies and BTC
Business API and webhook-oriented integrations
LNURL and Lightning Address support in current API flows
Product availability and fiat rails are jurisdiction-dependent
records.Verification basis: Current first-party API documentation verifies active Bitcoin/Lightning business payment functionality and the account/quote model.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not assume historic product behavior or country support remains current.

Strike's consumer app has wallet/exchange characteristics, but the canonical PAYMENTS inclusion is its integrated business/payment role; do not create a second WALLETS profile without Master Registry review.

records.Concise description: Square merchant acceptance feature that lets eligible sellers take Lightning Bitcoin payments at point of sale and settle the value into a Square Bitcoin balance or U.S. dollars.
records.Deeper researched summary: Square integrated Bitcoin acceptance into its existing merchant stack rather than creating a standalone Bitcoin wallet. Current U.S. support documentation describes Lightning QR payments, NFC tap on compatible second-generation Square Register hardware, optional BTC or USD settlement, and Bitcoin invoicing. The flow is a hosted Square merchant service: Square manages the merchant Bitcoin balance/settlement experience rather than simply generating an address to a merchant-controlled self-custody wallet.
Creators / founders: Square / Block product and engineering teams
records.Launch / history: Square began rolling Bitcoin acceptance to eligible U.S. sellers in the mid-2020s and expanded current merchant and invoice payment support through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: Square is one of the most significant examples of Bitcoin/Lightning acceptance being embedded into mainstream point-of-sale infrastructure rather than requiring a Bitcoin-native merchant stack.
Important technical or cultural characte: Lightning merchant acceptance
QR checkout and compatible NFC tap flow
Merchant settlement choice between BTC balance and USD
Integrated Square POS and invoice workflows
Hosted merchant account rather than direct self-custody settlement

Official sources.label: Square Support — Accept and manage bitcoin payments

records.Verification basis: Current official Square support documentation verifies active deployment, supported payment rail and settlement model as of 2026-08-15.
Research notes / uncertainties: Current availability is limited by seller eligibility and jurisdiction; do not publish a timeless geography statement.
Processing pricing, limits and hardware eligibility are time-sensitive and intentionally omitted from canonical copy.
Square Bitcoin Payments is a product capability inside Square; one integrated profile avoids separate POS/invoice duplicates.
